title: Plan data goes in, a guided session and updated weights come out

parts.name: Plan data (plan.json)
parts.description: The approved 12-week plan as data: three lift sessions with ordered blocks, every exercise's sets, rep range, effort target and rest, the stretch block, run definitions, the weekday calendar and the week phases. Changing the plan means editing this file and publishing a new version; no code changes. v1.4 adds a tempo and focus cues to every exercise and a goal sentence to every session. v1.5: exercises that use two dumbbells are marked pair, and every curl is named by type. v1.9: data/goals.json holds the ranked goals for the Plan tab, and data/muscles.json maps each exercise to muscle groups.

parts.name: Settings (settings.json)
parts.description: Defaults for cues (vibrate, beep, warning tick), screen wake lock, transition seconds, start date and bodyweight. Cameron's changes in the Settings screen are stored in IndexedDB on top of these defaults. v1.5: confirmSetup toggles the Set-up done tap before each new block.

parts.name: Cameron's taps
lines: Start, Done, edit a set, review,
parts.description: Everything Cameron does in the app: start a session, tap Done on a set, edit weight/reps/RPE, pause, skip a step, go back one step, trim to fit, end early, fill the run form, edit a target, back up, export, restore. v1.9: coach check-ins on the Plan tab: a note with quick tags (Too heavy, Too light, Rest too long, Need more rest, Pain, Slept badly, Felt good). Weight tags move that lift's next target one step; rest tags move its rest 15 s, at most 45 s either way (settings.restAdjust, applied by the Session Builder).

parts.name: Garmin runs
lines: activities from the watch, by way
of a job in your private repo
parts.description: Optional (v1.10). Garmin's personal API lets Cameron read his own activities with a key he creates in Garmin Connect. The key is saved as a secret in his private GitHub repo, where a small job (data/garmin-job.yml, added to that repo during set-up) asks Garmin every two hours, and whenever the app saves garmin-request.json there, and writes garmin-activities.json with the location fields dropped. The phone reads that file through the same token sync uses and adds what is new to the run log: runs, ski days and long bike or rower sessions (rules.json garmin.types). A run typed in by hand on the same day takes the watch's numbers instead of being logged twice, a deleted Garmin run stays out, and type, effort and notes are never overwritten. The key is never on the phone, in the app or in a backup. A computer set to Only views never adds runs; it shows them after the phone uploads. From v1.12 the app decides which planned run a Garmin run is (rules.json garmin.assign): an intervals signal from the watch or a long enough run settles it, otherwise the planned day, then whichever run is still open that week. Cameron's own pick of type always sticks.

parts.name: Rules (rules.json)
parts.description: Progression rules as data: weight increments per lift, the success test (all sets at the top of the range at RPE 8 or lower), the accessory rule (reps first, then the smallest jump), the stall rule (two misses, drop 10%), baseline weeks, phase overrides (week 7 half sets, weeks 8-11 at 3-5 reps, week 12 retest), ramp-up steps, trim order and timing estimates. v1.4 adds set timing (tempo default, margin, set-up seconds by equipment, get-ready seconds), the effort scale behind the four effort buttons (stored as RPE 6, 8, 9, 10), and rough starting-weight estimates for free-weight accessories. v1.5: dumbbellPairs (pair lifts are stored as totals and jump two dumbbell steps), timing.confirmSetup (wait for a tap before each new block), review.blockSaveOnOpenItems, weighted pull-up jump 5 lb. v1.8: catchUp (warm-up, rest for a lone superset exercise, stretch on or off).

parts.name: Session Builder
parts.description: Expands a session from plan.json into a flat, ordered list of steps: warm-up holds, ramp-up sets, work sets, rests, superset alternation (B1 set, short rest, B2 set, longer rest), finisher rounds, dead hangs, transitions, stretches. Fills each set's target weight and reps from the saved targets, applies the week's phase (baseline, light, heavy, retest) and estimates each step's planned seconds for the clock. Since v1.4 a set's seconds come from its reps and the exercise's tempo (plan.json) plus a margin, and every set has a countdown in front of it: the rest before it, a set-up step sized by equipment before an exercise's first set, or a short switch step inside finisher rounds.

parts.name: Player
parts.description: Walks the timeline one step at a time. Timers are computed from timestamps so they stay right when the screen locks. Vibrates and beeps when a rest ends, keeps the screen awake, shows planned vs projected finish and how far ahead or behind the session is, and offers Trim to fit (preview, then confirm). Each work set shows last session's result for that exercise. Logging a set runs a live PR check against the stored bests (estimated 1RM, heaviest weight) and gives a haptic tap. When the app is in the background during a rest, it asks the service worker to fire a notification at the end time. Pause, back and end early live behind the menu button; the in-progress session is saved on every step so it can be resumed. Since v1.4 a work set ends on its own timer and is logged at its target; the rest screen that follows shows the set just done with four effort buttons and a tap-to-fix weight and reps. The last 5 seconds before every set are a get-ready count (amber screen, ticks, the coming set spoken aloud). A pace bar shows which rep the tempo puts you on. The screen is green for work, blue for rest. Back and Pause are on the screen. Voice and auto-advance can be switched off in Settings. v1.5: Pause is in the header on every step with a tap-to-resume banner; the countdown before the first set of a new block holds until Set-up done is tapped; Equipment taken moves a later block to now and puts the current one right after it; in a finisher the top bar lists its exercises; the last-set card has - and + for weight and reps and a Logged / Saved check; two-dumbbell lifts show the total with 2 x each.

parts.name: Logger
lines: one tap logs weight, reps, RPE
parts.description: Records each set: Done accepts the pre-filled target weight and reps; Edit opens weight, reps and RPE. When the session ends it opens the Review screen: every exercise with its sets (tap to correct), the engine's verdict (Up / Hold / Drop / Set) with its reason, and the next weight and reps as editable fields; Save runs the engine on the corrected sets, applies any overrides (tagged 'set by you') and stores the session. Then the summary. The run log form moved to the Runs page in v1.10. v1.5: the Review screen lists skipped sets and sets missing a weight or reps first and keeps Save locked until each is filled in or confirmed as skipped.

parts.name: Progression Engine
lines: applies rules after review and save
parts.description: Runs once after a session saves. For each exercise in the session: applies the week override if any, the baseline rule in weeks 1-2, otherwise the success test (main lifts) or the reps-then-weight rule (accessories), counts stalls and drops 10% after two misses, computes Epley estimated 1RM for benchmark lifts, writes the new targets and a plain-language what-changed line per exercise. Power clean is excluded from automatic progression. Also keeps each exercise's best estimated 1RM and heaviest weight and reports personal records when a session beats them. v1.5: incrementFor doubles the jump for pair lifts; starting estimates for pair lifts are totals.

parts.name: Catch-up list
parts.description: Works out what is still owed this week from the saved sessions: sets that were skipped or never reached (a session ended early), minus any already made up, plus whole lifts whose day has passed with nothing logged. Sets cut by Trim to fit and the if-time block are not owed, and nothing carries past Sunday. From the leftover sets it builds a Catch-up session (short warm-up, the owed blocks in plan order, stretch) that the Session Builder turns into a timeline like any other. On a Slack day it takes the today card on Home; on other days it shows as Owed this week. Catch-up sets are logged and count for records; they move a target only for an exercise the original session never logged. Settings are in rules.json under catchUp.

parts.name: Storage and offline cache
parts.description: IndexedDB holds targets (with per-exercise bests for PR checks), sessions, runs, what-changed lists, settings overrides and the in-progress session. The service worker caches the app's files under a versioned cache name so it opens with no signal, picks up a new version on the next open with signal, and shows the rest-end notification when the page asks it to while in the background. Backup writes a JSON file with everything; Restore reads one back. v1.5: a pairTotals flag records whether older per-dumbbell numbers were doubled; the app asks once when it finds them, and a restored pre-v1.5 backup asks again.

parts.name: Architecture tab
parts.description: Draws this diagram from architecture.json and lists every part with its description. The search box filters parts and flows by any word. If a part is added, removed or renamed in code, this file changes in the same commit and the spec doc's diagram is redrawn to match.

parts.name: Guided session screen
parts.description: What Cameron sees at the gym: the current exercise, set number, target weight and reps, effort target, a countdown or count-up, what comes next, and the session clock. v1.5: Pause in the header, a Set-up done tap before each new block, Equipment taken, finisher exercises in the top bar, and a last-set card kept apart from Up next.

parts.name: Progress: sessions and exercises
parts.description: The Log tab lists past sessions (tap for all sets and what changed) and, in its Exercises view, every exercise with its sets by date, PR markers and an estimated-1RM trend line. The Home screen shows next targets (editable) and a Benchmarks table for the seven benchmark lifts: the benchmark you entered (a set of 5 with 2 reps left), current estimated 1RM, and the next target the plan derives from it. v1.9: the Log tab moved inside Progress as Sessions and Exercises next to Overview.

parts.name: Progress page
parts.description: The Progress tab, laid out for a computer screen and still usable on the phone: which planned lifts are done, ended early or missed in each of the 12 weeks, a chart of estimated 1RM per benchmark lift from each session's best set, personal records, work sets per week and each accessory's first and latest top set. It reads saved sessions and runs; it changes nothing. On a computer it offers Load backup file, which puts the phone's backup into that browser. v1.9: with one session a lift card shows the best set and the next target instead of a lone dot; clicking a card opens every set of that lift; a card for work sets per muscle group this week against what the plan holds and a 10-set mark (data/muscles.json); sync status moved to the header.

parts.name: Runs page
lines: this week's two runs and what each
asks for, miles by week, every run
parts.description: The Runs tab (rebuilt in v1.10). This week's planned runs with what each asks for: the interval set for the week and the long-run distance, one step past the longest long run so far (both from the numbers on plan.json runs). Each shows done with its numbers once a run is logged for it. Below: miles by week across the block (bike and ski distance left out, rules.json runLog), and every run with distance, time, pace and heart rate. Opening a run shows the watch's numbers and takes effort and what it counts as in one tap. Log a run takes time as 27:30. Garmin status, Check now and set-up sit under the heading. From v1.12 a run done on another day counts for the planned run it replaces, and a run not done yet says which days still work (rules.json runSchedule, never a lift day); Home shows it on the day it moved to.

parts.name: Backup and export
lines: JSON to Drive via share sheet,
sheet in the Log tab layout
parts.description: Back up opens the Android share sheet with the backup JSON so Cameron can save it to Drive > Training in one tap; Download saves it on a PC. Export builds an .xlsx with a Log sheet and a Runs sheet in the same columns as the Excel log, using SheetJS vendored in the repo.

parts.name: Sync to your private repo
parts.description: Optional, off until set up in Settings. Keeps one file (tracker-data.json, the same content as a backup) in a private GitHub repo that belongs to Cameron. The phone uploads a few seconds after every saved session, run, target or settings change, and retries when signal returns. A device set to Only views downloads the file when the app opens and never uploads. The repo name and token are stored on the device only and are not part of a backup. The app refuses a public repo, and an empty phone loads the existing copy instead of overwriting it. Nothing is written to the app's own repo. v1.9: the header shows sync status with a refresh button. Both devices also read coach.json from the same repo (written by the coach review); only the phone applies its adjustments, once each.
